label: Acts 24:1
text: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.

label: Acts 24:2
text: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that prosperity is coming to this nation by your foresight,

label: Acts 24:3
text: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

label: Acts 24:4
text: But, that I don’t delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.

label: Acts 24:5
text: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.

label: Acts 24:6
text: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.

label: Acts 24:7

variants.reading: The short text the WEB prints (24:6 'He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.' straight to 24:8 'By examining him yourself...'): the Western addition 24:6b-8a (Lysias rescuing Paul and commanding his accusers to come) is not printed.
variants.note: The runner brief and the book's known-omissions list state 24:6b-8a is absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' records 'Acts 24:6b-8a verse omitted by majority of the mss.'.

variants.reading: 24:6b-8a contained (with textual differences) in E (Codex Bezae), Psi, 056, 0142, 33, 88, 181, 424, 436, 483, 614, 630, 945, 1505, 2412, 2495
variants.note: Per the fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles'. The WEB therefore prints no verse 7 text; this passage node carries no codex preserves edges from Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, only Bezae.

label: Acts 24:8
text: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.”

label: Acts 24:9
text: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.

label: Acts 24:10
text: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, “Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,

label: Acts 24:11
text: seeing that you can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.

label: Acts 24:12

label: Acts 24:13
text: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.

label: Acts 24:14
text: But this I confess to you, that after the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;

label: Acts 24:15
text: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

label: Acts 24:16

label: Acts 24:17

label: Acts 24:18

label: Acts 24:19

label: Acts 24:20
text: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,

label: Acts 24:21
text: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!’”

label: Acts 24:23
text: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody, and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.

label: Acts 24:24
text: But after some days, Felix came with Drusilla, his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.

label: Acts 24:25

label: Acts 24:26
text: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often, and talked with him.

label: Acts 24:27
text: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.

label: The governor before whom the case was brought was Antonius Felix
statement: The 'governor' (hegemon) before whom Ananias and Tertullus informed against Paul was Antonius Felix, Roman procurator of Judaea.
note: Office/title claim, kept apart from the hearing event, per the brief's instruction and the precedent of claim:ac-17-06-politarchs.

label: After five days the high priest, elders and Tertullus came down and informed the governor against Paul
statement: After five days the high priest Ananias came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus, and informed the governor against Paul.
note: The delegation event itself is Acts-only; Josephus records Ananias's earlier trip to Rome (Ant. 20.131) but not this delegation.

label: Tertullus was an orator (rhetor) employed by the Jewish leaders
statement: Tertullus, named as the orator of the delegation, made a formal rhetorical presentation for the Jewish leaders against Paul.
note: Gap for the person: Tertullus is unattested outside Acts; the fetched Wikipedia 'Tertullus' article states he 'was an orator or lawyer who was employed by the Jewish leaders', generally assumed a Hellenistic Jew, possibly a Gentile. Office/title claim.

label: Professional advocates (rhetores) were hired to plead before Roman governors
statement: Hiring a professional advocate (rhetor) to present a case before a Roman governor was an established practice of the period.
note: Only modern references were fetchable (source:wikipedia-acts-24, source:wikipedia-tertullus); an ancient attestation (a classical text or documentary papyrus on advocates before provincial governors) would upgrade this.

label: Tertullus attributed peace and prosperity in Judaea to Felix's foresight
statement: Tertullus opened by claiming that through Felix the nation enjoyed much peace and that prosperity was coming by his foresight, accepting it with all thankfulness.
note: The flattery event is Acts-only; Josephus and Tacitus record the opposite condition under Felix (recorded with complicates).

label: Tertullus charged Paul with being a plague and an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews
statement: Tertullus charged that Paul was a plague, an instigator of insurrections (staseis) among all the Jews throughout the world.
note: The charge event is Acts-only. The contemporary seditious-impostor epidemic Josephus records (claim:ac-24-05-impostors-felix-era) is the condition making the charge plausible; linked related_to.

label: The followers of Jesus were called 'the sect of the Nazarenes' (Nazoraioi)
statement: Tertullus called the movement 'the sect of the Nazarenes' (haeresis ton Nazoraion) - the first known plural use of Nazoraioi for Christians as a group.
note: Title claim apart from the charge event. External evidence is reception (Tertullian, Against Marcion 4.8: Jews called Christians 'Nazarenes'; grade D) and the Birkat ha-Minim Geniza text naming notzrim/ha-nazarim (grade D; the date of the addition is disputed).

label: While Felix was procurator, impostors led crowds of Jews into the wilderness promising signs
statement: During Felix's procuratorship deceivers persuaded crowds to follow them into the wilderness promising wonders, and an Egyptian prophet led people to the Mount of Olives; Felix suppressed them by force (Josephus, Ant. 20.167-172).
note: Context claim: the sedition-plague that makes Tertullus's 'instigator of insurrections among all the Jews' charge intelligible. Same phenomenon as claim:ac-21-38-egyptian-4000 (the Egyptian); related_to.

label: Tertullus charged Paul with trying to profane the temple
statement: Tertullus charged that Paul tried to profane the temple, and that the Jews arrested him (in the Western addition: and would have judged him by their law, had Lysias not rescued him).
note: The same charge as Acts 21:28 (claim:ac-21-28-accusation), now made in a Roman court; the gravity of temple profanation rests on the exclusion custom (claim:ac-21-28-gentile-exclusion, attested by the Temple Warning inscription in data/acts/21).

label: Felix had been judge (governor) of the nation for many years
statement: Paul said he knew Felix had been a judge of this nation for many years, and cheerfully made his defense.
note: Josephus: Claudius sent Felix to Judaea in his twelfth year (52 CE); Wikipedia gives 52-60, so about eight years by the hearing. Tacitus: Felix 'had for some time been governor of Judaea'.

label: No more than twelve days had passed since Paul went up to Jerusalem to worship
statement: Paul said Felix could verify it was not more than twelve days since he went up to Jerusalem to worship.
note: A checkable chronology; no external evidence found.

label: Paul denied disputing or stirring crowds in the temple, synagogues or city
statement: Paul denied that he was found in the temple disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues or in the city, and said his accusers could not prove their charges.
note: Denial event; nothing external bears on it.

label: Believers were called 'the Way' (hodos), which opponents called a sect (hairesis)
statement: Paul confessed to serving the God of the fathers 'after the Way, which they call a sect' - 'the Way' as the movement's self-designation, 'sect' (hairesis) as opponents' label.
note: No external evidence fetched for the term's use; the Nazarene title (claim:ac-24-05-nazarenes) is the opponents' label for the same movement.

label: Paul hoped for a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and the unjust
statement: Paul said he had hope toward God - which his accusers also shared - that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
note: Paul's confession of a doctrine, not the doctrine itself. Daniel 12:2 is a biblical cross-reference (related_to only); the shared Pharisaic hope is claim:ac-24-15-pharisaic-resurrection.

label: Paul came to Jerusalem after some years bringing alms to his nation and offerings
statement: Paul said that after some years he came to bring gifts (eleemosynas) for the needy of his nation, and offerings.
note: Paul's collection for Jerusalem: biblical cross-references Romans 15:25-26 and 1 Corinthians 16:1-4 (related_to only).

label: Jews from Asia found Paul purified in the temple, without mob or turmoil
statement: Paul said certain Jews from Asia found him purified in the temple, not with a mob nor with turmoil.
note: Same purification-rite setting as claim:ac-21-26-purification-temple and the same Asian Jews as claim:ac-21-27-asian-jews-riot; related_to.

label: Paul said his Asian accusers ought to have been present to make their accusation
statement: Paul argued that the Jews from Asia, who had found him, ought to have appeared before the governor to accuse him if they had anything against him.
note: Procedural point; no external evidence.

label: Paul said his present accusers should state what injustice they found when he stood before the council
statement: Paul challenged his accusers to say what injustice (adikema) they found in him when he stood before the council (the Sanhedrin of Acts 23).
note: Back-reference to the council hearing of Acts 23; the 24:20 wording itself has a recorded variant (P74, א, A, B for the shorter reading).

label: Paul cried before the council that he was being judged concerning the resurrection of the dead
statement: Paul said that unless it was for this one thing he cried standing among the council - 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged by you today' - they had no charge.
note: Same resurrection dispute as 23:6; the doctrine is claim:ac-24-15-pharisaic-resurrection.

label: Felix, having more exact knowledge of the Way, deferred the case until Lysias came down
statement: Felix adjourned the hearing, saying he would decide when Lysias the commanding officer (chiliarch) came down; he had a more exact knowledge concerning the Way.
note: No external evidence; Felix's familiarity with Judaea's affairs is context from his long tenure.

label: Felix ordered the centurion to keep Paul in custody with privileges, letting friends serve him
statement: Felix ordered the centurion to keep Paul in custody but with some indulgence (anesin), not forbidding his friends to serve him or come to him.
note: No external evidence fetched for such relaxed custody of a prisoner before a governor.

label: Drusilla, Felix's wife, was a Jewess, daughter of Herod Agrippa I
statement: Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess (Ioudaia); Josephus identifies her as the daughter of Agrippa I, who left Azizus king of Emesa to marry Felix.
note: Person claim kept apart from the hearing event. Josephus is A; Tacitus (Hist. 5.9) names Drusilla as Felix's wife but identifies her as a granddaughter of Antony and Cleopatra - the identification tension is on a complicates edge.

label: Felix with Drusilla sent for Paul and heard him about faith in Christ
statement: After some days Felix came with Drusilla and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
note: Event; Acts-only.

label: Felix was terrified by Paul's talk of righteousness, self-control and judgment, and dismissed him
statement: As Paul reasoned of righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified (emphobos) and answered 'Go your way for this time; when I have a convenient season I will call you'.
note: Event; Acts-only.

label: Felix hoped Paul would give him money and sent for him often
statement: Felix hoped that money would be given to him by Paul to release him, and for that reason sent for him more often and talked with him.
note: The bribe hope is Acts-only; Tacitus's portrait of Felix's base exercise of power ('every kind of barbarity and lust... the power of a king in the spirit of a slave') supports the character trait at C.

label: Porcius Festus succeeded Felix as procurator of Judaea
statement: When two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus.
note: Office/title claim kept apart from the two-year chronology. Josephus, Ant. 20.182: 'Porcius Festus was sent as successor to Felix by Nero' (A).

label: Paul was left in custody two years, to Felix's recall and Festus's succession, c. 58-60 (date debated)
statement: Acts dates the succession to 'two years fulfilled'; the absolute date of Festus's succession is disputed: most scholars opt for 58-60, Bruce argues 59 from a change in the provincial coinage of Judaea attested for Nero's fifth year, Conybeare and Howson argue 60.
note: D: the date is debated, per the fetched Wikipedia 'Porcius Festus'. Josephus attests the succession itself but gives no date. Felix's own coinage under his administration is dated year 3 of Nero (56/57) in the fetched caption.

label: Felix, wanting to do the Jews a favor, left Paul in bonds
statement: Felix, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, left Paul in bonds when his term ended.
note: Event; Acts-only. Josephus records Felix's Caesarean troubles but says nothing of Paul's detention.

label: Felix was recalled to Rome to answer accusations of the Caesarean Jews and escaped through Pallas's intercession
statement: The principal Jewish inhabitants of Caesarea went up to Rome to accuse Felix, who would have been punished had Nero not yielded to the importunate solicitations of his brother Pallas (Josephus, Ant. 20.182).
note: The recall behind 'Felix was succeeded'; brief grades it B (Josephus is the sole direct source and partly an insider's apology for the Herodian circle).

label: Paul (Saul of Tarsus)
note: First mention at Acts 7:58 as the young man at whose feet the witnesses laid their garments; later Acts chapters reuse this node.

label: Porcius Festus (procurator of Judaea)
dates: procurator of Judaea after Felix; the date is disputed, most scholars 58-60
note: Named by Josephus as sent by Nero as Felix's successor (Ant. 20.182); his prutah coinage is dated year 5 of Nero (58/59).

label: Drusilla (Julia Drusilla, daughter of Herod Agrippa I)
aka: Julia Drusilla; Drusilla the Jewess of Acts 24:24
dates: AD 38 - AD 79 (Wikipedia); sister of Berenice and Agrippa II
note: Married Azizus king of Emesa, then left him for Felix (Josephus, Ant. 20.141-144); their son Agrippa died in the Vesuvius eruption of 79.

note: Unattested outside Acts; the fetched Wikipedia article states he was an orator or lawyer employed by the Jewish leaders, generally assumed a Hellenistic Jew, possibly a Gentile.

label: Ananias son of Nedebaeus (high priest c. 47-59 CE)
note: Appointed high priest by Herod king of Chalcis (Josephus, Ant. 20.103); sent in bonds to Rome to answer Quadratus (Ant. 20.129-130); under Albinus a 'great hoarder up of money' whose servants took the priests' tithes by violence (Ant. 20.205-206). Whiston's note identifies him as the high priest before whom Paul pleaded.

label: Antonius Felix (procurator of Judea, c. 52-59 CE)
note: Brother of the freedman Pallas; Claudius 'sent Felix, the brother of Pallas, to take care of the affairs of Judea' (Josephus, Ant. 20.137); Tacitus, Hist. 5.9: he 'exercised the power of a king in the spirit of a slave'; Annals 12.54: he thought 'he could do any evil act with impunity'; recalled and nearly punished, saved by his brother Pallas (Ant. 20.182-184).

label: Drusilla was Felix's wife, a Jewish Herodian princess (Agrippa I's daughter)
statement: Drusilla, who came with Felix to hear Paul, was Felix's wife and a Jewess - the daughter of Agrippa I, given first to Azizus king of Emesa and then married to Felix while he was procurator.
